mainTopic: Refused gifts and ריש לקיש's rule, then the laws of an אשם תלוי or אשם ודאי that turns out to be unneeded, and when an עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden.
overview: The גמרא finishes testing ריש לקיש, who holds that a refused gift belongs to no one, so whoever grabs it first acquires it. It defends him against three sources: "his words stand," "my hand is removed from this field," and a ברייתא about refused slaves eating תרומה. The last one is answered with the rule that a slave made ownerless still needs a גט שחרור, and until he gets it he eats תרומה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about an אשם תלוי that turns out to be unneeded. It explains רבי אליעזר's view by linking it to the Sages who told בבא בן בוטא to wait for a real doubt. Next it deals with the burning versus burying of unneeded offerings. רבה calls the משנה a תברא, and רב אשי explains the burning as being only because the meat looks like a disqualified offering. It then explains why the meat may be eaten if the truth comes out after the blood is sprinkled, and gives two explanations of רבי יוסי's view. Finally, it brings a dispute between רב המנונא and רבא about when an עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden, and asks רב המנונא from what moment the איסור starts.

steps.title: Does "his words stand" mean the gift goes back to the owner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא's phrase דבריו קיימין means the refused gift returns to its original owner, which would contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't "his words stand" mean that the item goes back to its owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא it just quoted in a way that seems to prove ריש לקיש wrong. It suggests the refused gift simply goes back to the giver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says a refused gift becomes ownerless, so anyone who grabs it wins. If "his words stand" means the refusal works and the item returns to the giver, then the gift is not ownerless at all. That would be a direct contradiction of ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: "What, is it not...?" A way of proposing a reading of a source in order to prove a point
"His words stand," meaning his statement takes effect
It goes back to its owner

phrases.english: What, is it not that "his words stand"
means that it returns to its owner?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the attack on ריש לקיש from the ברייתא cited just before this section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a refused gift is ownerless and anyone who grabs it acquires it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "his words stand" means the item returns to the giver, the refused gift is not ownerless.

steps.title: "His words stand" can mean the gift is ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. "His words stand" means that even the original owner does not get the item back, so it is ownerless and whoever grabs it acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. "His words stand" means he too does not acquire it, and anyone who takes hold of it acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by reading the same phrase differently. The refusal works, so the recipient does not own the item, but nobody else owns it either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "his words stand" only tells us the refusal is effective. It does not tell us where the item goes next. Read this way, the ברייתא fits ריש לקיש perfectly: the item is ownerless, like הפקר.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not acquire it
One who takes hold of it, taking possession of it physically
He acquires it

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's position: when a gift is refused, it belongs to no one, and the first person to grab it owns it.

phrases.english: No, "his words stand"
means that he too does not acquire it,
phrases.notes: "He" here means the original owner. Not even he gets the item back.

phrases.english: and anyone who takes hold of it acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּבָרָיו קַיָּימִין – וְהוּא נָמֵי לָא קָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by offering a different reading of the same phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "His words stand" means the gift returns to the giver.
steps.terutzMaskana: "His words stand" means the refusal works and even the original owner does not get it back, so the item is ownerless and anyone may grab it.

steps.title: Challenge: "my hand is removed from it" achieves nothing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who declares "I have no claims on this field" or "my hand is removed from it" has said nothing. Since "my hand is removed" sounds like אי אפשי, this seems to contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who tells his fellow, "I have no claims on this field," "I have no business with it," or "My hand is removed from it" has said nothing. But "my hand is removed" is just like "I don't want it," and it says he said nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש. In it, a person who says "my hand is removed" from a field does not give it up at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "My hand is removed from it" sounds the same as "I do not want it." Yet the ברייתא says this statement has no effect. If saying אי אפשי really makes something ownerless, as ריש לקיש says, why does this similar phrase do nothing?

keyTerms.meaning: Legal claims and dealings
Business or involvement
"My hand is removed," meaning I am withdrawing myself
"I do not want it"
He has said nothing, so his words have no legal effect

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who says to his fellow:

phrases.aramaic: ״דִּין וּדְבָרִים אֵין לִי עַל שָׂדֶה זוֹ״,
phrases.english: "I have no claims or dealings regarding this field,"
"I have no business with it,"
or "My hand is removed from it"
has not said anything.
But "My hand is removed from it"
is like "I do not want it,"
and yet it teaches: he has not said anything!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was deflected, a new source is brought against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that saying אי אפשי makes the item ownerless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "My hand is removed" is the same as אי אפשי, yet the ברייתא says it has no effect at all.

steps.title: He only gave up legal claims, not the field itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this case is different. The person only removed himself from legal claims, not from ownership of the field itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. He is saying that he removed himself from claims and dealings; from the field itself he did not remove himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by narrowing what the speaker in that ברייתא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In context, "my hand is removed" is attached to "claims and dealings." So he is only saying he will not argue or go to court about the field. He never said he does not want the field itself, so this is not a true case of אי אפשי.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is different there," a way of showing a source does not apply to our case
He removed himself
The field itself, the actual property

phrases.english: It is different there, for he is saying:
when he removed himself, it was from claims and dealings;
from the field itself he did not remove himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "My hand is removed from it" equals a full refusal of the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only gave up legal claims, not ownership of the field, so it is not a true case of אי אפשי.

steps.title: New challenge: slaves in a gift that the recipient refused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a man who wrote his property, including slaves, over to someone who said "I do not want them." The תנא קמא says that if the recipient is a כהן, the slaves eat תרומה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the heirs already acquired them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who writes his property over to another, and there were slaves among it, and the other says "I do not want them": if the second master is a כהן, they may eat תרומה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: once he said "I do not want them," the heirs have already acquired them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins another challenge to ריש לקיש by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the problem; the גמרא will spell out exactly how it challenges ריש לקיש next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither opinion seems to say the refused slaves become ownerless. The תנא קמא treats them as still belonging to the recipient, so they eat תרומה if he is a כהן. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives them to the giver's heirs, as if the gift went back to the giver's side.

keyTerms.meaning: One who writes his property over to someone, as a gift in writing
Their second master, the recipient of the gift
The priestly portion of produce. A כהן's slaves are allowed to eat it
Heirs, here the heirs of the one who gave the gift

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two masters. The "second master" is the one who received the gift, and the "heirs" are the giver's heirs.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who writes his property over to others
and there were slaves among them,
and the other one said: "I do not want them,"
if their second master was a priest
phrases.notes: The "second master" is the man who received the gift. The first master was the giver.

phrases.english: they may eat teruma.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
once he said: "I do not want them,"
the heirs have already acquired them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second challenge was answered, a third source is brought against ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a refused gift becomes ownerless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, neither opinion treats the refused slaves as ownerless. One leaves them with the recipient, and the other gives them to the giver's heirs. The גמרא will spell out the full argument next.

steps.title: The slave case works for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but not for the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל fits easily, because a refused gift goes back to the giver. But for the תנא קמא, if a refused item becomes ownerless as ריש לקיש says, the slaves would be non-כהנים, so how can they eat תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He holds that a person gives a gift only on the condition that it is accepted, so if it is refused, it goes back to its owner. But what about the תנא קמא? If saying 'I do not want them' makes the item ownerless, then here the second man said 'I do not want them.' So the slaves are non-כהנים, and non-כהנים would be eating תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the challenge from the ברייתא of step 5. It shows that the problem is only with the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a refused gift goes back to the giver, so nothing is ownerless and there is no question. But the תנא קמא lets the slaves eat תרומה. If ריש לקיש is right that a refused item becomes ownerless, the slaves would belong to no כהן and should not be allowed to eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted', meaning this view causes no problem (a different view will)
With the intention of, on the understanding that
It returns to its owner
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Non-כהנים, who may not eat תרומה

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
he holds: when a person gives a gift,
it is on the understanding that it will be accepted from him;
when it is not accepted from him,
it goes back to its owner.
But according to the first tanna,
if, when one says 'I do not want them,'
anyone who takes hold of them acquires them,
then here, where the second man said 'I do not want them,'
phrases.notes: The 'second' is the person the slaves were written over to.

phrases.english: they are non-priests,
and non-priests are eating teruma!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly why the ברייתא quoted in step 5 is a problem for ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a refused item becomes ownerless, as it fits the תנא קמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the refused slaves are ownerless, they belong to no כהן, yet the תנא קמא says they eat תרומה.

steps.title: A slave set free still needs a document, and until then he eats תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that a slave made ownerless is free but still needs a document of freedom. Until he gets it, he may still eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds that a person who makes his slave ownerless has set him free, but the slave still needs a document of freedom from his master. And he also holds that a slave who is only held back by not yet having that document still eats תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps ריש לקיש's rule. It explains why the slaves may still eat תרומה even though they were given up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a slave ownerless frees him, but the freedom is not complete until he gets a document of freedom. While he waits for that document, he keeps the status of a כהן's slave for eating תרומה. So the ruling of the תנא קמא does not disprove ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives up ownership of his slave
Goes free
A document that frees a slave
Held back, still waiting

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule survives: the slaves eat תרומה only because a freed slave stays in his old status until he receives a גט שחרור.

phrases.english: He holds: one who gives up ownership of his slave,
the slave goes free,
but he needs a document of freedom from his master,
and he holds: one who is held back only for a document of freedom
eats teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ownerless slaves are simply non-כהנים and cannot eat תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: An ownerless slave who still lacks a גט שחרור keeps his right to eat תרומה, so ריש לקיש's rule stands

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר in the משנה about the אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה: רבי אליעזר says the אשם תלוי is still offered even after the person learns he did not sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אליעזר says: It should be offered, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting רבי אליעזר's words from the משנה. It is setting up a question about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in the משנה is a person who set aside an אשם תלוי and then found out he never sinned. רבי אליעזר says the animal is still offered anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
It should be offered

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It should be offered, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gift and slave topic and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the אשם תלוי is still offered even when the person learns he did not sin

steps.title: Why does רבי אליעזר need a sin at all?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה suggests the offering comes to atone for some other sin. But רבי אליעזר elsewhere says one may bring an אשם תלוי every day as a voluntary gift, so why mention any sin?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, why do I need a sin? Didn't רבי אליעזר say an אשם תלוי can come as a voluntary gift? As we learned: רבי אליעזר says a person may volunteer an אשם תלוי every day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reasoning given for רבי אליעזר in the משנה. It does so by quoting another statement of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, the reason the offering is still brought is that it will atone for some other sin. But in another משנה, רבי אליעזר lets a person bring an אשם תלוי daily with no sin at all. If so, why does he need any sin to justify bringing it?

keyTerms.meaning: A sin
A voluntary gift offering
Volunteers to bring an offering

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, why do I need a sin?
phrases.notes: The משנה's reason was that the animal atones for some other sin; the גמרא asks why that is needed.

phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
a provisional guilt offering can come as a voluntary gift?
As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בְּכׇל יוֹם!
phrases.english: A person may volunteer a provisional guilt offering every day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind the משנה quoted in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's idea that the offering needs some other sin to atone for
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר elsewhere allows an אשם תלוי as a pure gift, so a sin should not be needed.

steps.title: This רבי אליעזר follows the Sages who told בבא בן בוטא to wait
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that our משנה follows the Sages who said an אשם תלוי needs a real situation of doubt, not רבי אליעזר's own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The רבי אליעזר here follows the view of 'those who said to him.' As we learned: 'But they said to him: Wait until you enter a situation of doubt.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He says the משנה here follows a different opinion than רבי אליעזר's view about daily gift offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other משנה, רבי אליעזר reports that בבא בן בוטא brought an אשם תלוי every day, but the Sages told him to wait until there was a real doubt. Our משנה follows those Sages, who do not allow an אשם תלוי as a pure gift. That is why a sin is needed here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Those who said to him', meaning the Sages who disagreed with בבא בן בוטא
Wait
A situation of doubt about whether one sinned

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם תלוי as a pure gift is a disputed idea; our משנה follows the Sages who require a real doubt, so a sin is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Those who said to him' are not רבי אליעזר himself. They are the Sages who answered בבא בן בוטא, and רב אשי says our משנה follows them.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This Rabbi Eliezer follows 'those who said to him,'
phrases.notes: 'Him' is בבא בן בוטא, who wanted to bring this offering every day.

phrases.english: as we learned: But they said to him:
Wait until you come into a situation of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאָמְרוּ לוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the משנה to a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה follows רבי אליעזר's view that an אשם תלוי may be a daily gift
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows the Sages who require a real doubt, so the offering needs some sin to atone for

steps.title: The meat of an unneeded אשם תלוי is burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if a person learns after the slaughter that he did not sin, the meat of the אשם תלוי is burned. The גמרא learns from this that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he found out after the animal was slaughtered that he had not sinned, the meat goes out to be burned. So we see that non-holy animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard must be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and draws a general rule from it. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once it is clear there was no sin, the animal seems to be just חולין that was slaughtered in the עזרה. Since the משנה says to burn it, the גמרא concludes that such animals are burned, not buried.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where disqualified holy things are burned
Evidently / so we see
Non-holy animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: If after it was slaughtered it became known, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about the אשם תלוי. The person found out he never sinned at all.

phrases.english: It teaches: the meat shall go out to the place of burning.
Evidently, non-holy animals slaughtered in the courtyard are burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי הַבָּשָׂר יֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה אַלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה about an אשם תלוי that turns out to be unneeded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this line of the משנה, חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are burned.

steps.title: The אשם ודאי case says to bury the animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if an אשם ודאי turns out to be unneeded after it was slaughtered, it is buried. That suggests חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are buried, not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a contradiction: a definite אשם is not like this. If he found out before it was slaughtered, it goes out and grazes with the flock. If he found out after it was slaughtered, it must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction from a later line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unneeded אשם ודאי also looks like חולין slaughtered in the עזרה. But here the משנה says to bury it, not burn it. So the two lines seem to give opposite rules for the same kind of animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction between sources
A definite guilt offering, brought for a sin the person knows he did
It must be buried

phrases.english: But a contradiction was raised: a definite guilt offering is not so.
If he found out before it was slaughtered,
it goes out and grazes among the flock;
if after it was slaughtered, it must be buried!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule learned in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה says an unneeded אשם ודאי, which also looks like חולין slaughtered in the עזרה, is buried.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: two different תנאים wrote this משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה is a תברא. One תנא wrote one line and a different תנא wrote the other line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: this משנה is broken. The one who taught this line did not teach that line.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction by saying the two lines come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two different תנאים wrote the two lines, there is nothing to fix. One holds such animals are burned, and the other holds they are buried.

keyTerms.meaning: A broken (split) משנה, where its parts follow different תנאים

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: The one who taught this did not teach that

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: it is broken;

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: the one who taught this did not teach that.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּבְרַאּ מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two lines come from different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought one תנא taught the whole משנה, so it seemed to contradict itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different תנאים taught the two lines, so they can disagree.

steps.title: רבה: the two kinds of אשם are not the same
steps.stepSummary: רבה says you cannot compare an אשם ודאי to an אשם תלוי. The אשם ודאי was never truly made holy, so it is plain חולין. The אשם תלוי was truly made holy, so it is a disqualified holy animal and is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Are you comparing a definite אשם to a doubtful אשם? A definite אשם: since he turns out not to need it, he never really made it holy. A doubtful אשם: since his heart bothers him about a possible sin, he fully decides to make it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects the contradiction. He shows the two cases are different, so this is not the place to say the משנה is a תברא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an אשם ודאי, the owner only made it holy because he thought he had to. Once it turns out he did not need it, it was never holy, so it is חולין and is buried. With an אשם תלוי, his worry makes him fully commit, so it stays holy and is burned like any disqualified holy animal. The burning teaches nothing about חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: You are raising a contradiction
A provisional guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure if he sinned
His heart bothers him (he feels worried)
He fully decides and makes it holy

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are burned. He is saying the אשם תלוי is not חולין at all. It is a holy animal that cannot be used, and that is why it is burned.

phrases.english: Rabba said: a definite guilt offering
against a provisional guilt offering you are raising a contradiction?

phrases.aramaic: אָשָׁם וַדַּאי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא צְרִיךְ לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: A definite guilt offering, since he does not need it,
he did not make it holy.
A provisional guilt offering, since his heart strikes him,
he fully resolves and makes it holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָשָׁם וַדַּאי עַל אָשָׁם תָּלוּי קָרָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissolves the contradiction in step 12, so the תברא of step 13 is not needed to settle it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The contradiction between the אשם תלוי line and the אשם ודאי line.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question assumed both animals are חולין. Only the אשם ודאי is חולין; the אשם תלוי stays holy.

steps.title: The real problem: two rules inside the אשם ודאי case
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the real contradiction is inside the אשם ודאי case. After slaughter it is buried, but after its blood is sprinkled the meat is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a problem, it is the definite אשם against the definite אשם. The משנה says it must be buried. But the next line says: the meat goes out to be burned!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה points to a contradiction that his answer cannot solve. Both lines are about the same אשם ודאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, an unneeded אשם ודאי is plain חולין, and sprinkling its blood does not make it holy. So in both lines it is חולין slaughtered in the עזרה. Yet one line says to bury it and the next says to burn it.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty
Say the last part (of the משנה)

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty,

phrases.aramaic: אָשָׁם וַדַּאי עַל אָשָׁם וַדַּאי קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: a definite guilt offering against a definite guilt offering is difficult,
since it teaches: it must be buried;

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וְהַבָּשָׂר יֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵיפָה!
phrases.english: say the last part: and the meat goes out to the place of burning!
phrases.notes: This last part is about finding out only after the blood was already sprinkled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After removing the first contradiction, רבה points to a different one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two rules in the משנה about an unneeded אשם ודאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same חולין animal is buried in one line and burned in the next.

steps.title: So the משנה really is a תברא
steps.stepSummary: Because of the contradiction inside the אשם ודאי case, רבה agrees the משנה is surely a תברא written by different תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is certainly a broken משנה: the one who taught this line did not teach that line.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה concludes that רבי אלעזר's answer is right, but for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה showed that the first contradiction can be solved without a תברא. But the burying and burning inside the אשם ודאי case cannot be solved that way. So different תנאים must have written these lines.

keyTerms.meaning: This one certainly

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: an unneeded אשם ודאי was never truly holy, while an unneeded אשם תלוי was fully made holy and is burned. In his view, the משנה is still a תברא because of the conflict between burying and burning within the אשם ודאי rules. The next step brings רב אשי, who explains the burning without needing a תברא.

phrases.english: This is certainly broken;

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: the one who taught this did not teach that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is a תברא. Different תנאים disagree about whether חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are buried or burned.

steps.title: The meat is burned only because it looks like a disqualified offering
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the burning of the meat in the first line of the משנה is no contradiction. It is burned because it looks like a disqualified offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The first line, which says about an אשם תלוי, 'the meat goes out to the place of burning,' is not difficult. The meat is burned because it looks like a disqualified offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different way to solve the contradiction, so the משנה does not have to be a תברא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the משנה must be a תברא, because the meat is buried in one case and burned in another. רב אשי says the burning does not prove the meat is truly holy. It is burned only because it looks like a disqualified offering. That means the rule that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are buried can still stand, and one תנא can be behind the whole משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
It looks like; it appears as
A disqualified offering, whose meat must be burned
The place where disqualified holy things are burned

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the משנה as one unified teaching instead of splitting it between two תנאים.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The first clause, which teaches about a provisional guilt offering:
"And the meat shall go out to the place of burning" –
is not difficult,
because it looks like a disqualified offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רֵישָׁא דְּקָתָנֵי בְּאָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction that רבה solved by calling the משנה a תברא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reason reinterpretation: the burning is about appearance, not about real holiness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning the meat means the animal is truly holy, which goes against burying it in the other case
steps.terutzMaskana: The meat is burned only because it looks like a disqualified offering, so there is no real contradiction

steps.title: Why may the meat be eaten if he now knows the truth?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the blood was sprinkled, the meat is eaten. The גמרא asks why, since the person now knows the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If the blood was sprinkled, the meat may be eaten. But why? He now has knowledge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought only when a person is unsure whether he sinned. Here he found out the truth, so the doubt is gone. If the reason for the offering is gone, why should its meat still be eaten as a proper offering?

keyTerms.meaning: The blood was sprinkled on the מזבח
Knowledge; finding out what really happened
Why?

phrases.english: If the blood was sprinkled – the meat shall be eaten.
But why?
He now has knowledge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the meat of the אשם תלוי is eaten after the blood was sprinkled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אשם תלוי needs doubt. Once he knows the truth, the doubt is gone, so the offering should lose its purpose.

steps.title: What counts is the moment of forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the פסוק: the person must not know at the time of forgiveness, which is when the blood is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, 'And he did not know, and he shall be forgiven.' This person did not know at the time of forgiveness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by reading a פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'he did not know' right next to 'he shall be forgiven.' So the doubt has to exist at the moment of forgiveness, which is when the blood is sprinkled. Here he found out only after the sprinkling, so the offering already did its job, and the meat may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall be forgiven
The time of forgiveness, when the blood is sprinkled

steps.whatToRemember: For an אשם תלוי, what matters is that he did not know at the moment of sprinkling. Finding out afterward does not ruin the offering.

phrases.english: Rava said: The verse states:
"And he did not know, and he shall be forgiven,"
and this one did not have knowledge
at the time of forgiveness.
phrases.notes: The forgiveness happens when the blood is sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אֲמַר קְרָא: וְהוּא לֹא יָדַע וְנִסְלַח לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a פסוק that sets the key moment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any knowledge, even after sprinkling, cancels the אשם תלוי
steps.terutzMaskana: Only knowledge before the moment of forgiveness matters; here it came after, so the meat is eaten

steps.title: Why does רבי יוסי let the blood be sprinkled?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the blood is sprinkled even if he found out while it was still in the cup. The גמרא asks why, since now he knows at the time of forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even if the blood is still in the cup, and so on. According to רבי יוסי, why should it be sprinkled? He has knowledge at the time of forgiveness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's view in the משנה and challenges it using רבא's rule from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא just said the person must not know at the time of forgiveness. In רבי יוסי's case, he found out before the blood was sprinkled. So at the moment of forgiveness he already knows, and by רבא's rule the sprinkling should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood is in the cup, collected but not yet sprinkled
It shall be sprinkled

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even if the blood is in the cup, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei, why should it be sprinkled?

phrases.aramaic: הָא הָוְיָא לֵיהּ יְדִיעָה בִּשְׁעַת סְלִיחָה!
phrases.english: He has knowledge at the time of forgiveness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's rule from step 19 to challenge רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling that the blood in the cup is still sprinkled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבא's rule, he must not know at the time of sprinkling. Here he already knows before sprinkling, so it should not be sprinkled.

steps.title: Blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יוסי follows רבי שמעון: anything standing ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוסי holds like רבי שמעון, who said: Anything that is ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was already sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by connecting רבי יוסי to a known rule of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood was in the cup, it was ready to be sprinkled. רבי שמעון treats such blood as if it were already sprinkled. So in a sense the forgiveness already happened before he found out, just like in the case of step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever stands ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled
Holds like; follows the opinion of

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds like Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: כׇּל הָעוֹמֵד לִיזָּרֵק – כְּזָרוּק דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: who said: Whatever is ready to be sprinkled – is treated as if sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the view to another תנא's principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood was not yet sprinkled, so he knew before forgiveness
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood ready to be sprinkled counts as sprinkled, so the forgiveness counts as done before he found out

steps.title: This blood was never really ready to be sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבי שמעון's rule is only for blood that truly will be sprinkled, but this blood was not going to be sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that רבי שמעון said his rule about something that is ready to be sprinkled. But this blood is not ready to be sprinkled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's answer by limiting רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's rule works when the blood is certainly going to be sprinkled. Here the person found out the truth before sprinkling, so the blood was never truly headed for the מזבח. So the rule does not fit this case, and רבי יוסי's view still needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; you could argue that
It is not ready to be sprinkled

phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Shimon said this
about something that is ready to be sprinkled,
but this, it is not ready to be sprinkled!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, בְּמִידֵּי דְּעוֹמֵד לִיזָּרֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי שמעון's rule to explain רבי יוסי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule only applies to blood that will surely be sprinkled; this blood was not going to be

steps.title: A holy vessel makes even a disqualified offering fit to be brought
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל say רבי יוסי holds that a כלי שרת makes even a disqualified offering holy enough to be brought from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West: רבי יוסי holds that service vessels make even a disqualified offering holy, so that it may be brought from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבא's answer was rejected, a new answer from ארץ ישראל explains רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if this blood lost its purpose once he found out the truth, it was already collected in a holy vessel. In רבי יוסי's view, the כלי שרת makes it holy enough that it is offered from the start, even though it is disqualified. So the blood is sprinkled for a different reason, not because of רבי שמעון's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Holy service vessels of the בית המקדש
Make holy
Something disqualified
To be offered from the start, not just after the fact

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי lets the blood be sprinkled because, in his view, a כלי שרת makes even a disqualified offering fit to be brought from the start.

phrases.english: They say in the West:
Rabbi Yosei holds:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ אֶת הַפָּסוּל
phrases.english: service vessels make the disqualified thing holy
to be offered even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to step 20 after רבא's answer was rejected in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: New underlying principle attributed to the תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רבי שמעון's rule, there is no reason to sprinkle blood that lost its purpose
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלי שרת makes even the disqualified blood fit to be offered from the start, so it is sprinkled

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a definite guilt offering is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: an אשם ודאי is not treated like the אשם תלוי that was just discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a definite guilt offering is not like that, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next line. This sets up the discussion that follows about the עגלה ערופה, which the משנה lists in the same breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the משנה dealt with an אשם תלוי that can still be brought after the person finds out he did not sin. Now the משנה says an אשם ודאי works differently, and the full line also includes the עגלה ערופה. The גמרא writes only the opening words and expects us to know the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: A definite guilt offering, brought when a person knows for sure that he sinned
Short for 'and so on'. The rest of the quoted line continues from here

phrases.english: A definite guilt offering is not so, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה line adds that an עגלה ערופה is also different. If the killer is found before its neck is broken, it goes out to graze. If he is found after, it is buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוסי / אשם תלוי discussion and opens the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם ודאי (and an עגלה ערופה) is not treated like an אשם תלוי once the doubt is cleared up.

steps.title: Dispute: when does the heifer become forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says an עגלה ערופה is forbidden for benefit already while alive. רבא says it becomes forbidden only after its neck is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: from when is an עגלה ערופה forbidden? רב המנונא says: from while it is alive. רבא says: after its neck is broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between two אמוראים about the moment the עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the עגלה ערופה ends up forbidden for benefit. The only question is timing. רב המנונא says the איסור starts while the animal is still alive. רבא says it starts only once the neck is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
Becomes forbidden, meaning no one may get any benefit from it
From while it is still alive
Breaking the neck of the heifer

phrases.english: It was stated:
A heifer whose neck is broken, from when is it forbidden?
phrases.notes: Forbidden here means forbidden to get any benefit from it.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna says: from while it is alive,
Rava says: after the breaking of its neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's mention of the עגלה ערופה with a dispute about when its איסור begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב המנונא: forbidden from while alive. רבא: forbidden only after the neck is broken.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya will test each view, starting with what exact moment רב המנונא means.

steps.title: For רב המנונא, from what moment?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's view has a clear moment, the breaking of the neck. For רב המנונא, the גמרא asks what exact moment while the animal is alive makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to רבא: the איסור starts from the time an action is done to it. But according to רב המנונא, from when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב המנונא. Since nothing has been done to the living animal, what point makes it forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא there is a clear event that creates the איסור: the act of breaking the neck. רב המנונא says it is forbidden while alive, but he does not name any event. The גמרא demands that he point to a specific moment.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense. Opens a question: one view works fine, but the other is hard
An action done to the animal, here the breaking of its neck

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava,
it is from the time that an action was done to it;
phrases.notes: The action is the breaking of the neck.

phrases.english: but according to Rav Hamnuna, from when?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא מֵעִידָּנָא דְּאִיתְעֲבִיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֶׂה, אֶלָּא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא, מֵאֵימָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's side of the dispute just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's view that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden while still alive.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An איסור needs a clear starting point. רבא has one, the act of breaking the neck. רב המנונא does not name one, so it is unclear when the living animal becomes forbidden.
